extracted.intended_audience: general readers; students and practitioners of journalism and media studies
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and evaluating the features, effects, and criticisms of the 24-hour/24-7 news production cycle across television, radio, print, online and mobile media. Includes definitions, historical context, and critique of impacts on journalistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 24-hour news cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: The 24-hour news cycle (or 24/7 news cycle) is the 24-hour investigation and reporting of news, concomitant with fast-paced lifestyles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies across television, radio, print, online and mobile app news media; driven by many suppliers wanting to be relevant and deliver news first to remain ahead of competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete news cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete news cycle consists of the media reporting on some event, followed by the media reporting on public and other reactions to the earlier reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process has been considerably shortened by 24-hour cable/satellite channels and web-based news sources (including blogs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed / pace of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A high premium on faster reporting emerged with 24-hour news and online news, leading to a much faster pace of news production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster reporting shortens the time available for verification and may create tensions between speed and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition for audience and advertiser attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Vast news resources have increased competition for audience and advertiser attention, prompting media providers to deliver the latest news in the most compelling manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being first and compelling is often prioritized as a strategy to remain ahead of competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification (traditional journalistic value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification is named as a traditional journalistic value that has declined under the pressures of the 24-hour news environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kovach and Rosenstiel cite verification as one of the values threatened by competition and profit pressures; maintaining verification is presented as a quality criterion for journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion (traditional journalistic value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion is listed among traditional journalistic values (alongside verification, relevance, depth, quality of interpretation) that may be lost under 24-hour news pressures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proportion refers to appropriate weighting and context of coverage; its erosion signals disproportionate focus or sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance (traditional journalistic value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance is identified as a core journalistic value potentially undermined by the drive for constant updates and attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reporters should assess whether rapidly pushed content is genuinely relevant to the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth (traditional journalistic value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depth of reporting is highlighted as a value that can decline in a 24-hour news environment focused on continuous, rapid updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depth entails thorough reporting and interpretation rather than superficial or repeated coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of interpretation (traditional journalistic value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of interpretation is named as a journalistic standard threatened by speed and competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality interpretation provides context and meaning beyond immediate facts and should be preserved despite time pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensationalism / entertainment / opinion (negative shift)
rubrics_metrics.description: The press has moved toward sensationalism, entertainment, and opinion — trends presented as departures from traditional journalistic values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tendencies are framed as negative outcomes of the 24-hour cycle and profit pressures; they are cited as markers of declining journalistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism of assertion (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Journalism of assertion" is described as a practice that de-emphasizes whether a claim is valid and encourages putting a claim into the arena of public discussion as quickly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as an undesirable model encouraged by the 24-hour cycle; avoidance of this practice (favoring verification and validation) is implied as a standard.
